introduction.title: Understanding Chord Progressions
introduction.text: Chord progressions are the backbone of all popular music. They create emotional journeys, establish keys, and provide the harmonic framework that melodies and rhythms build upon. Understanding how and why certain progressions work will unlock the language of harmony and help you recognize patterns across all genres.

columns.title: Harmonic Foundation
columns.text: Creates the emotional and tonal framework for songs

columns.title: Functional Movement
columns.text: Each chord has a role in creating tension and release

columns.title: Emotional Impact
columns.text: Different progressions evoke distinct emotional responses

cards.title: Tonic (I)
cards.description: Provides harmonic stability and sense of resolution

fields.label: Typical Usage
fields.value: Song beginnings, endings, points of rest

cards.title: Subdominant (IV)
cards.description: Moves away from tonic, provides gentle contrast

cards.title: Dominant (V)
cards.description: Creates tension that demands resolution to tonic

fields.label: Typical Usage
fields.value: Ends of phrases, before choruses, climactic moments

cards.title: I-V-vi-IV (Pop Progression)
cards.description: The most popular progression in modern music

fields.label: Theory
fields.value: Strong tonic establishment, dominant tension, deceptive resolution to vi, plagal motion back

cards.title: vi-IV-I-V (Emotional)
cards.description: Starts melancholy, builds to bright resolution

fields.label: Theory
fields.value: Minor beginning creates vulnerability, major progression builds hope and energy

cards.title: I-vi-IV-V (50s Progression)
cards.description: Classic doo-wop and early rock progression

fields.label: Theory
fields.value: Smooth voice leading, natural harmonic rhythm, perfect for loops

items: Stand By Me - Ben E. King

fields.label: Theory
fields.value: Strongest possible cadential motion, ii prepares V which resolves to I

fields.label: Theory
fields.value: Perfect cadential motion demonstrating all primary harmonic functions

fields.label: Theory
fields.value: Minor start creates darkness, repeated dominants build tension for eventual resolution

cards.title: 1. Identify the Key
cards.description: Determine the tonal center of the song

fields.label: Process
fields.value: Listen for the chord that feels like "home" - usually the first or last chord

fields.label: Example
fields.value: If the progression feels resolved on C major, the key is C major

cards.title: 2. Number the Chords
cards.description: Assign Roman numerals based on scale degrees

fields.label: Process
fields.value: Count up from the tonic: I, ii, iii, IV, V, vi, vii°

fields.label: Example
fields.value: In C major: C=I, Dm=ii, Em=iii, F=IV, G=V, Am=vi, B°=vii°

cards.title: 3. Identify Functions
cards.description: Determine the harmonic role each chord plays

fields.label: Process
fields.value: Group chords by function: Tonic, Subdominant, Dominant

cards.title: 4. Analyze Movement
cards.description: Study how chords progress and create momentum

fields.label: Process
fields.value: Look for patterns: circle of fifths, stepwise motion, functional progression

fields.label: Example
fields.value: V-I creates strongest resolution, IV-I creates plagal cadence

cards.title: Descending Fifths
cards.description: Creates strong forward momentum. Very common in jazz and sophisticated pop music. Each chord naturally leads to the next.

cards.title: Ascending Fifths
cards.description: Creates building energy and brightness. Common in rock and pop for building excitement toward choruses or climaxes.

exercises.title: Listening Practice
items: Listen to popular songs and identify the chord progressions
Notice how different progressions create different emotions
Practice hearing the difference between major and minor chords
Identify when songs use the same progression in different keys
Listen for functional movement: tonic → dominant → tonic

exercises.title: Playing Practice
items: Learn each progression in multiple keys
Try playing progressions with different chord voicings
Write original melodies over familiar progressions
